thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-proxy p99 tail latency > 1.2s and spike in client reconnects observed for us-east-1. Start=1977778888 UTC, impact: streaming stalls + reconnect loops. Auto-page: dutch-oncall.

alice.sre: seeing p95 at ~450ms but p99s shooting to 1.2-1.8s, and an uptick in TLS handshake failures in the logs.

ben.netops: seeing a correlated increase in NAT ephemeral port exhaustion and SYN retransmits across AZ-a -> AZ-c paths. Packetloss ~0.3% on some flows.

carmen-prod: customer reports: several long-polling websocket sessions dropped and clients auto-reconnect; UX shows replay/dup messages. Severity: customer-facing for a subset of streaming tenants.

dutch-oncall: acked, jumping in. Initial mitigation checklist: 1) confirm scope (regions/azs) 2) attempt NAT pool scale / reroute 3) short-term flow-steering to alternate AZs.

eva-support: which tenants impacted? I can surface IDs and recent error rates into the incident doc.

alice.sre: list looks concentrated on us-east-1 AZ-c and AZ-d, ~12% of streaming connections for those tenants. Slower elsewhere. Logs show TLS handshake timeouts and some DNS retries prior to connect.

ben.netops: running quick query on edge-proxy telemetry: `SELECT count(*) WHERE region='us-east-1' AND (tls_handshake_ms>500 OR reconnects>0) GROUP BY az` -> AZ-c 7k, AZ-d 5.5k, AZ-b 1.2k.

netops-bot: auto-run: increased SNAT pool on us-east-1 from 4096 -> 16384 on nodes tagged streaming-proxy-*. Completed in 30s.

alice.sre: rolled a small routing tweak to prefer local egress for AZ-c to avoid hairpin paths; monitoring.

carmen-prod: customer escalations incoming. ETA for visible improvement?

dutch-oncall: give it 2-5 minutes; if no improvement, plan B: divert new sessions to us-east-2 replicas and enable fail-open short-circuit for existing streams.

eva-support: notifying top 5 affected customers now (template: "We're investigating elevated streaming disconnects in us-east-1; engineering is actively mitigating.").

alice.sre: metrics: reconnects down 40% after SNAT bump, but p99 still ~1.0s. Seeing fewer TLS handshake errors but some long tail remains, trace samples show repeated DNS lookup latency spikes from proxy to internal resolver (~200-800ms).

ben.netops: launching a quick DNS path check and will force node-level resolver cache purge on affected proxies. Command: `sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved` (rolling).

netops-bot: notice: restarting resolver on streaming-proxy-azc-12, -13, -14 (rolling, 10s gap).

alice.sre: after resolver restart, TLS handshake timeouts drop considerably. p99 down to ~650ms, reconnects down to baseline for most tenants, but a small tail persists for long-lived sessions.

carmen-prod: customers reporting fewer reconnects, one reporting still-seen stalls on long sessions (>30s).

dutch-oncall: next steps: 1) keep resolver restarts rolling for any remaining nodes 2) schedule short-lived graceful drain of worst-hit proxies and shift traffic 3) create runbook entry for DNS/resolver-induced streaming stalls.

ben.netops: root cause hypothesis: intermittent resolver timeouts under load + SNAT pool pressure causing handshake retries and backoff that amplifies tail latency. Followup: investigate resolver metric shard, upstream resolver health, and NAT port reuse pattern.

alice.sre: filed follow-up ticket INF-4821 with traces, hotspot nodes, and remediation timeline. Assign to netops and infra.

oncall-next: I'm taking next shift for the postmortem and will own customer comms until resolved. any handoff notes?

dutch-oncall: handoff: key mitigations applied: SNAT increase, resolver restarts, local egress routing preference. Monitor for 2 hours; if p99 < 700ms and reconnects < 2x baseline, we close paging.

eva-support: will consolidate customer updates and mark impacted tenants in the incident doc.

alice.sre: adding short-term dashboard widgets (p95/p99, reconnect rate, TLS handshake errors, DNS latency) to incident board.

ben.netops: next-day action items: increase SNAT pool headroom for streaming fleet, harden resolver scaling, add health-checks for TLS handshake latency, and build autoscale for short-lived NAT capacity.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigations applied, severity reduced. Recording timeline: start=1977778888, mitigations=1977778889..1977778900, monitor window starts now.

oncall-next: thanks all — I'll update the incident channel with the postmortem link once the follow-ups are scheduled. :white_check_mark:
